site.name: Atelier Mirza Reza
site.concept: Portfolio of Mirza Reza Tabrizi, a contemporary tile-mosaic and architectural ornament practitioner working in the Safavid tradition.

card_pattern: Each project card is a square-ish module set on a lapis-dark surface, framed by a thin gold ogee-arch outline with a small palmette flourish at the apex. The interior holds a centered project title in Cinzel Decorative caps over a turquoise rule, with a short body paragraph in Cormorant Garamond and a discreet date/medium line in gold small-caps at the foot. Cards align in axial pairs separated by an arabesque filet divider, never edge-to-edge with the page.
design_rules: Compositions are strictly axial and symmetrical, with cobalt fields broken by ivory-cream cartouches and gold ornament concentrated at borders, corners, and arch apexes. Pattern density alternates heavy and light — no even tiling across full pages — and ornament reads as cut-tile mosaic rather than painted line. Color stays inside the cobalt-turquoise-gold-ivory axis; accents are sparing and never decorative for its own sake.

pages.title: Atelier Mirza Reza — Tile-Mosaic & Architectural Ornament
pages.content_brief: Iwan-tall hero with a centered ogee-arch portrait of the workshop's signature commission, the Naqsh-e Jahan vestibule restoration (2019). Beneath the arch, a calligraphic banding line reads 'Workshop of Mirza Reza Tabrizi — Established Isfahan, 2007'. Three brief cartouches introduce the practice: tile mosaic (haft-rang and moarraq), stucco muqarnas, and architectural consultation. Closing tailpiece links into the portfolio.

pages.title: Selected Works — Atelier Mirza Reza
pages.content_brief: Grid of eight project cards, each in a gold-outlined ogee frame: 'Vestibule of the House of Sheikh Bahā'ī' (2019, moarraq tile, Isfahan), 'Mihrab Spandrel, Masjid-e Nour' (2021, Yazd), 'Chehel Sotoun Mirror Panel Replacement' (2022, ayina-kari), 'Private Garden Pavilion, Kashan' (2023), 'Sabzeh Meidan Fountain Surround' (2018), 'Bonyad Library Reading Iwan' (2020, Tehran), 'Embassy of Oman Reception Wall' (2024), and 'Hammam Vault Restoration, Shiraz' (2017). Each card carries year, technique, and city.

pages.title: On Method — Atelier Mirza Reza
pages.content_brief: Long-form essay describing the workshop's method, from cartoon-drawing on grid paper to firing of seven-color tiles at 920°C and final assembly on lime-gypsum (gach) backing. Walk through the four stages: tarrahi (design), borideh-kari (cutting), chideman (laying), and band-keshi (grouting). Include a sidebar on the master-apprentice line from Ostad Hossein Lorzadeh through Mirza Reza's teacher, Ostad Mahmoud Farshchian-Yazdi.

pages.title: The Maker — Atelier Mirza Reza
pages.content_brief: Biographical page on Mirza Reza Tabrizi (b. 1974, Tabriz). Trained at the Isfahan School of Traditional Arts, 1992–1998. Apprenticed eight years under Ostad Mahmoud Farshchian-Yazdi at the Sheikh Lotfollah conservation campaign. Founded the atelier in 2007 in the Jolfa quarter, Isfahan. Includes a short list of teaching residencies (Royal College of Art, 2016; Aga Khan Academy, 2019; Met Museum visiting fellowship, 2022) and a closing ornament.

pages.title: Press & Honours — Atelier Mirza Reza
pages.content_brief: Chronological list of publications and awards: 'A Living Tilework' — Apollo Magazine, March 2023; 'The Last Mosaicists of Isfahan' — Aramco World, July 2021; UNESCO Living Human Treasure nomination, 2020; Tehran Triennial of Traditional Crafts, gold medal, 2018; entry in 'Persian Tile in the Twenty-First Century' (Thames & Hudson, 2024, ed. Sussan Babaie). Each row is set in a small cartouche separated by arabesque filets.

pages.title: Studio & Commissions — Atelier Mirza Reza
pages.content_brief: Contact and commissions page. Studio address: Atelier Mirza Reza, 14 Kucheh-ye Khaju, Jolfa, Isfahan 8174693311, Iran. Hours by appointment, Saturday through Wednesday, 9:00–17:00. Telephone +98 31 3627 4418. Correspondence: studio@atelier-mirzareza.ir. Brief commissioning note: minimum project scope 4 m² of tilework; lead time 6–14 months; cartoons and material samples prepared on agreement. Closing centered seal with a final tailpiece.
